summary.title: New Threat Model - OnlineShop-ThreatModel
summary.description: Online shopping web application — customer storefront, checkout, authentication, and admin catalog management, per SWE420 Lab 05 scenario.

threats.title: Admin catalog change repudiation
threats.description: Admin denies making an unauthorized catalog change (e.g., price manipulation), with no non-repudiable record of admin actions.
threats.mitigation: Log every admin action with unique admin identity, timestamp, and before/after values; require re-authentication (step-up auth) for sensitive catalog changes.

threats.title: Customer credential spoofing
threats.description: Attacker uses stolen/guessed credentials, credential stuffing, or phishing to log in as a legitimate Customer and place fraudulent orders.
threats.mitigation: Enforce MFA on customer accounts; CAPTCHA + progressive delay/rate-limit on the login endpoint; monitor for credential-stuffing patterns.

threats.title: Payment amount tampering
threats.description: Attacker on the network path, or via a compromised endpoint, alters the payment amount or order total between the Web Application and the Payment Gateway.
threats.mitigation: Enforce TLS 1.3 with certificate validation/pinning for all Web App–Payment Gateway traffic; sign payment requests (HMAC) and verify integrity end to end; reconcile order total server-side after gateway response.

threats.title: Checkout action repudiation
threats.description: A customer denies placing an order or receiving a refund, and there is no verifiable record tying the action to their authenticated session.
threats.mitigation: Centralized, tamper-evident audit log (order id, timestamp, authenticated user id, source IP) with integrity protection (append-only store / hash chaining).

threats.title: Card data interception
threats.description: Card data or payment tokens are intercepted in transit or accidentally logged in plaintext by the Web Application, violating PCI-DSS.
threats.mitigation: Never store or log raw card data — use the gateway's tokenization; enforce TLS everywhere; keep the Web Application out of the PCI cardholder data environment.

threats.title: Storefront DDoS
threats.description: Volumetric DDoS against the public storefront makes the site unavailable to customers during high-traffic sale events.
threats.mitigation: Deploy behind a CDN/WAF with DDoS protection and auto-scaling; rate-limit at the edge; capacity-test before major sales.

threats.title: Unauthorized admin catalog access
threats.description: A regular authenticated Customer exploits a missing server-side role check (e.g., insecure direct object reference on an admin endpoint) to gain admin-level catalog access.
threats.mitigation: Enforce server-side RBAC on every admin endpoint (never trust client-side hiding of admin UI); isolate the admin panel on a separate authenticated path/network segment; least-privilege service accounts.

threats.title: Unauthorized direct database modification
threats.description: If database-level access controls are weak, an attacker who compromises the Web Application or gains network access to the database tier could modify Product Database records directly, bypassing the Admin panel's business logic and approval checks entirely.
threats.mitigation: Enforce network segmentation so only the Web Application's service account can reach the Product Database; apply least-privilege DB permissions (no direct admin/root access); enable DB-level audit logging for all write operations.

threats.title: SQL injection on customer records
threats.description: SQL injection through a storefront form lets an attacker directly modify customer order or address records.
threats.mitigation: Parameterized queries / ORM everywhere; strict server-side input validation; least-privilege DB account for the Web Application (no schema-altering rights).

threats.title: Customer PII exposure
threats.description: Customer PII (addresses, order history) exposed via a misconfigured database, an over-permissioned query, or an unencrypted backup.
threats.mitigation: Encrypt data at rest (AES-256); restrict DB network access to the application subnet only; mask/redact PII in logs; encrypt backups and restrict access to them.

threats.title: Session token spoofing
threats.description: Attacker forges or replays a session token (e.g., predictable token, missing signature check) to impersonate an authenticated user without valid credentials.
threats.mitigation: Issue short-lived, cryptographically signed tokens (JWT/opaque + server-side store); verify signature on every request; rotate/invalidate on logout and privilege change.

threats.title: Login endpoint brute-force DoS
threats.description: Attacker floods the login endpoint with authentication attempts (brute force / credential stuffing), exhausting service resources and blocking legitimate logins.
threats.mitigation: Rate-limit and progressively delay repeated failed logins per account/IP; deploy a WAF/bot-mitigation service; CAPTCHA after a failure threshold.

threats.title: Session token role tampering
threats.description: A flaw in session-token validation lets a low-privilege user modify a client-readable role claim to escalate to admin privileges.
threats.mitigation: Use signed tokens and verify the signature server-side on every request; never trust client-supplied role/permission claims; keep authoritative role data server-side only.
